posExamples.sentence: When the teacher asked who would like to visit the sick classmate, hands shot up all over the room like spring bamboo after rain. （读后续写·班级温情·比喻）
I still remember how you teased me for being the shortest in Grade 7 — well, I have shot up ten centimetres since then, and I can't wait to stand back-to-back with you this summer! （应用文·给笔友的信·亲切语气）
As screen time shoots up among teenagers, face-to-face conversations, once the glue of family life, are quietly slipping away. （议论文·科技与生活）
Orange flames shot up into the night sky, and within minutes the whole village was awake, buckets and blankets in hand. （读后续写·火灾·众人救援）

wordForms.other: 构成：shoot(v.)+up(adv.)，短语动词，不规则变化 shoot up-shot up-shot up。近义短语动词 go up/rise/climb(上升)。注意：主谓一致看真实主语——prices shoot up（复数）/ the number ... shoots up（单数）。

collocations.translation: 【课件】（人）快速长高，蹿个儿（grow rapidly）
collocations.example: Alan has shot up since I saw him last year. 自从去年见到艾伦以来，他个子蹿高了。（课件原句）
Prices of vegetables in this area shot up last year. 去年这一地区的蔬菜价格猛涨。（课件原句）
Flames were shooting up into the sky. 火焰腾空而起。（课件原句）

collocations.translation: 个子蹿高，快速长高（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: ... shooting up in height or getting left far behind. ……个子猛长，或被远远落在后面。（课文原句）

collocations.translation: 价格/成本飞涨（高考高频，不止"长个儿"）
collocations.example: Vegetable prices shot up after the flood. 洪灾后蔬菜价格飞涨。
Dozens of hands shot up the moment the chance was announced. 机会一宣布，几十只手齐刷刷举起。
Orange flames shot up into the night sky. 橙红的火苗蹿向夜空。
Her temperature shot up at midnight. 她的体温在半夜骤升。
The number of applicants shot up this year. 今年申请人数猛增。

synonyms.example: House prices have soared beyond the reach of ordinary young couples. 房价飙升到普通年轻夫妇负担不起。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：soar 偏书面，强调持续攀升至高位；shoot up 更口语，强调突然、迅速地上蹿。句法：prices soar；soar to a record high。

synonyms.example: Sales of the hand-warmer skyrocketed as the cold wave swept the country. 寒潮席卷全国，暖手宝销量暴涨。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：skyrocket/rocket 取"火箭式蹿升"之喻，速度感最强，多用于价格、销量；shoot up 还可用于长个儿、举手等具体动作。句法：多作不及物动词。

synonyms.example: Applications for the programme surged after last year's success. 去年成功后，项目申请量激增。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：surge 原义"浪涌"，兼指情绪、人流、数量的猛增；shoot up 更突出直线上蹿的画面感。句法：surge in sth / a surge of。

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·shoot up 用法族
advancedExpressions.expression: shoot up in height（长高）｜ prices shoot up（飞涨）｜ hands shoot up（举手）｜ flames shoot up（蹿火）｜ temperature shoots up（骤升）
advancedExpressions.example: 同一 shoot up，主语不同覆盖"长高/涨价/举手/蹿火/升温"多个高考场景，核心义都是"急速上蹿"。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能：表"急剧上升/增长"（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: shoot up ｜ soar ｜ skyrocket ｜ surge ｜ rise sharply ｜ climb rapidly
advancedExpressions.example: 写"数据猛增"可替换升级：the number rose → the number shot up / soared / surged（均可接 from ... to ...）。

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had ... than hands / cheers shot up ...
advancedExpressions.example: No sooner had the coach finished his question than a forest of hands shot up, each waving more eagerly than the next. （no sooner 倒装 + a forest of hands 比喻，集体场景）

advancedExpressions.expression: the number of ... has shot up from ... to ..., which ...
advancedExpressions.example: The number of students joining our morning-run club has shot up from a dozen to over two hundred, which speaks for the growing awareness of health on campus. （数据对比 + which 非限定性从句点评）

advancedExpressions.expression: with ... shooting up at an unprecedented speed, ...
advancedExpressions.example: With the amount of information shooting up at an unprecedented speed, the real skill of our era is no longer collecting facts but filtering them. （with 复合结构开篇 + no longer...but... 转折立论）

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many students raised their hands.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The question had barely left the teacher's lips when hands shot up across the classroom, eager fingers stretching towards the ceiling as if to touch the answer itself. （读后续写·课堂热情·夸张）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: barely...when 时间结构 + shoot up 动态替换 raise + as if 夸张想象收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: The price of vegetables increased quickly after the storm.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In the wake of the storm, vegetable prices shot up overnight — a sharp reminder of how fragile the link between weather and our dinner tables can be. （议论文·由现象到评论）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: in the wake of 高级介词短语 + overnight 强化速度 + 同位语(a sharp reminder...)由事及理

classPractice.question: 青春期的男孩常常几乎一夜之间个子猛长。Boys in puberty often ____ ____ in height almost overnight.
classPractice.note: shoot up in height=个子蹿高，还原课文用法；一般现在时表习惯，主语复数用原形。

classPractice.question: 用 shoot up/soar 之一填空并变形：After the flood, vegetable prices ____ overnight, forcing many families to change their shopping habits.
classPractice.note: "价格飞涨"是 shoot up 的高频引申义；叙述过去事件用过去式 shot up。

classPractice.question: The moment the volunteer chance was announced, dozens of hands ____ (shoot) up all over the room.
classPractice.note: shoot up 不规则：shot up-shot up；此处 hands shoot up=纷纷举手，过去时用 shot。

translation: 粉刺；斑点；污渍；地点，场所
sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: You might worry about your changing voice, weight problems or spots.
readingExamples: You might worry about your changing voice, weight problems or spots.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a small round mark or stain on a surface, especially one of a different colour
(2) n. a small red mark on the skin; a pimple
(3) n. a particular place or area, especially a pleasant one or one used for a particular purpose
(4) v. to see or notice sb/sth, especially suddenly or when it is not easy to do so

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】spotted 有斑点的，弄污了的（be spotted with 满是……斑点/污渍）
uncommonMeanings.example: His shirt was spotted with oil. 他的衬衫上满是油污。We lay on the grass, staring at the sky spotted with twinkling stars. 我们躺在草地上，仰望缀满闪烁繁星的天空。（课件原句）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】spotless 无脏污的，一尘不染的；无可挑剔的
uncommonMeanings.example: The kitchen was spotless from top to bottom. 厨房上下打扫得一尘不染。（课件配套词）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 粉刺，青春痘（皮肤上的小红点，课文本义，常用复数 spots）
uncommonMeanings.example: Teenagers troubled by spots on their faces should not feel ashamed. 为脸上痘痘发愁的青少年不必羞愧。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 斑点，污渍（表面上不同颜色的小圆点/污迹）
uncommonMeanings.example: There was a spot of ink on the white shirt. 白衬衫上有一点墨渍。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 地点，场所（尤指宜人或特定用途的地方）
uncommonMeanings.example: They found a quiet spot by the lake. 他们在湖边找到一处静谧的地方。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 发现，认出，注意到（尤指突然或不易察觉时，高考最爱考的僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Emma finally spotted a familiar red scarf in the crowd. 艾玛终于在人群中认出那条熟悉的红围巾。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （队伍、名单、节目中的）位置，名额
uncommonMeanings.example: Only two spots remained on the debate team. 辩论队只剩两个名额。

posExamples.sentence: They found a quiet spot by the lake, where willow branches trailed in the water and the afternoon seemed to slow down just for them. （读后续写·环境描写·静谧）

Situated at the foot of Purple Mountain, this scenic spot offers not only breathtaking views but also a vivid history lesson, which is why I recommend it as the first stop of your Nanjing tour. （应用文·推荐信）
Teenagers troubled by spots on their faces should remember that these small marks are simply proof of growing up, not flaws to be ashamed of. （议论文·青春期心态）
It takes a trained eye to spot the difference between genuine kindness and polite performance, but time reveals everything. （议论文·识人·警句风格）

wordForms.adjective: spotted (有斑点的) / spotless (一尘不染的)
wordForms.other: 拼写特例：spot 作动词时重读闭音节，双写 t——spot-spotted-spotted，现在分词 spotting。派生：spotless(spot+less=没有污点的→一尘不染的)、spotlight(聚光灯；公众关注)。名词短语记 on the spot(当场)、a soft spot for(偏爱)、a blind spot(盲区)。

idioms.example: The judges were so impressed by her improvised speech that they offered her the scholarship on the spot. （读后续写·高光时刻）
The reporter's blunt question put the young official on the spot, yet he handled it with surprising grace and honesty. （读后续写·从容应变）
Stern as he appeared, Mr. Zhang had a soft spot for students who dared to ask 'stupid' questions. （读后续写·师者仁心）
Finding himself in a tight spot — no map, no signal, and night falling fast — Leo forced himself to recall every survival tip his father had taught him. （读后续写·野外遇险）

collocations.translation: 【课件】斑点，污渍，点子（表面上不同颜色的小圆点）
collocations.example: His jacket was covered with spots of mud. 他的上衣满是泥点。I felt a few spots of rain. 我感觉掉雨点了。（课件原句）
The old town has become a popular tourist spot. 这座古城已成为热门旅游景点。（课件原句）
The man who tried to steal the lady's purse was caught on the spot. 那个想偷女士钱包的人当场被抓。An ambulance was on the spot within minutes. 几分钟之内，一辆救护车便赶到现场。（课件原句）
The journalist sent back an on-the-spot report from the flooded village. 记者从被淹的村庄发回现场报道。（课件原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】一点点麻烦（a spot of=少量的）
collocations.example: He's in a spot of trouble. 他遇到一点麻烦。（课件原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】发现某人正做某事（v.发现义）
collocations.example: After several hours, he finally spotted his team leader in the crowd. 几个小时后，他终于在人群中发现了自己的队长。（课件原句）
A careful proofreader can spot a mistake at a glance. 细心的校对员一眼就能发现错误。（课件原句）

collocations.translation: 为青春痘/粉刺发愁（课文原句词块，spots=青春痘）
collocations.example: You might worry about your changing voice, weight problems or spots. 你可能会为变声、体重问题或青春痘而烦恼。（课文原句）
Mr. Zhang had a soft spot for curious students. 张老师特别偏爱爱提问的学生。
Popular tourist spots are packed during the holiday. 假期里热门景点人满为患。
The rooftop garden proved the perfect spot for our English corner. 屋顶花园是我们英语角的绝佳地点。
Every driver has blind spots. 每个司机都有视觉盲区。
After circling the block three times for a parking spot, Dad joked that finding one downtown deserved a medal. （读后续写·生活幽默）
Careful readers will spot the subtle difference between 'hearing' and 'listening' — and therein lies the secret of communication. （议论文·细节之辨）
Amid the gloomy weeks of the flu season, the daily balcony concerts became the brightest spot of neighbourhood life. （读后续写·暖心亮点）

synonyms.example: Nobody noticed the new girl quietly wiping the blackboard. 没人注意到新来的女孩在默默擦黑板。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：notice 泛指"注意到"，最中性；spot 强调在不易察觉时"一眼认出/发现"，带惊喜或敏锐意味。句法：notice sb doing / spot sb doing。

synonyms.example: Rounding the corner, I caught sight of my lost dog. 拐过街角，我瞥见了走失的狗。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：catch sight of 突出"刹那瞥见"的瞬间性；spot 可含搜寻之后终于发现的过程感。句法：catch sight of + 名词。

synonyms.example: The crew searched for months for the ideal location. 剧组找了几个月才定下理想的取景地。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：location 较正式，指选定的位置；spot 口语化，常指具体的小范围地点（野餐、钓鱼的好去处）。句法：a filming location / a picnic spot。

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·spot 名词短语家族
advancedExpressions.expression: on the spot（当场）｜ put sb on the spot（让人当场为难）｜ have a soft spot for（偏爱）｜ a blind spot（盲区）｜ a bright spot（亮点）｜ in a tight spot（困境）
advancedExpressions.example: 一个 spot 撑起一串高频短语：搭配一变，义随之变，务必成组记忆。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能：表"（突然）发现/认出"（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: spot ｜ notice ｜ catch sight of ｜ catch a glimpse of ｜ pick out
advancedExpressions.example: 写"在人群中认出某人"可替换升级：I saw her → I spotted / caught sight of her in the crowd。

advancedExpressions.expression: it was ... that sb. spotted ..., and in that instant ...
advancedExpressions.example: It was among the sea of strangers that Amy spotted the little girl's yellow umbrella, and in that instant all her exhaustion melted into relief. （强调句+in that instant 情绪转折，寻人/重逢场景）

advancedExpressions.expression: boasting ..., ... is widely rated as the ideal spot for ...
advancedExpressions.example: Boasting a 600-year history and shaded stone paths, the ancient town is widely rated as the ideal spot for those seeking to escape the hustle and bustle. （boasting 分词开头+is widely rated as 推荐句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is easy to spot ..., but far harder to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is easy to spot the faults in others, but far harder to turn the same searching light upon ourselves. （对比结构+隐喻(searching light)，警句式开篇）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I saw my mother in the crowd.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The moment I stepped off the train, I spotted her in the surging crowd — my mother, on tiptoe, waving both arms as if I might somehow miss the brightest face on the platform. （读后续写·重逢·特写镜头）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: spot 替换 see 显敏锐 + 破折号特写(on tiptoe, waving both arms) + as if 从句写母爱之切

sentenceUpgrade.original: This is a good place for a picnic.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Nestled between the river bend and a chorus of old camphor trees, the meadow is arguably the finest picnic spot our city has kept secret from the guidebooks. （应用文·景点推荐·拟人）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Nestled 分词开头写位置 + a chorus of 拟人通感 + arguably 委婉最高级 + kept secret from 拟人收尾

classPractice.type: 写出画线词词性及中文（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: On the way, we spotted a man holding a piece of paper that said, "Lost my job. Family to Feed." 画线词 spotted 的词性及中文是？
classPractice.note: 【课件】spot作动词，spotted为过去式，意为"（不易察觉时）看见、发现、认出"。

classPractice.type: 写出画线词词性及中文（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: Jack showed me the exact spot where he had asked Rose to marry him. 画线词 spot 的词性及中文是？
classPractice.note: 【课件】spot作名词，意为"地点、场所"；the exact spot=确切的地点。

classPractice.type: 语法填空（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: We lay on the grass, staring at the sky ____ (spot) with twinkling stars.
classPractice.note: 【课件】the sky (which was) spotted with ...，过去分词作后置定语，be spotted with=满是……斑点。

classPractice.type: 完成句子（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: 我打算找一个更好的地点露营。I'm going to ____ ____ ____ ____ for us to camp.
classPractice.note: 【课件】spot作名词=地点；find a better spot=找一个更好的地点。

classPractice.question: Scanning the crowded platform, Emma finally ____ a familiar red scarf. (spotted / stared / glanced)
classPractice.note: spot(v.)=在不易察觉时一眼发现/认出，高考高频僻义；stared/glanced 无"发现"义。

classPractice.question: So impressed were the judges that they offered her the prize ____ ____ ____. (当场)
classPractice.note: on the spot=当场、立即，spot 的名词短语；注意与 put sb on the spot(使为难)区分。

classPractice.question: 严厉归严厉，张老师却对爱提问的学生格外偏爱。Stern as he was, Mr. Zhang ____ ____ ____ ____ ____ students who loved to ask questions.
classPractice.note: have a soft spot for sb/sth=对……特别喜爱/偏爱，固定搭配。

translation: (攻击的)目标，对象；靶子；把…作为攻击目标；面向
sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your anger.
readingExamples: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your anger.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a person, place or thing that is deliberately chosen to be attacked, criticized or affected by something
(2) n. a result or level that you aim to achieve within a fixed period of time
(3) n. an object, such as a board marked with circles, that you try to hit in shooting practice or archery
(4) vt. to aim an action, product or attack at a particular person or group

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （攻击、批评的）目标，对象（the first target of anger，课文本义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Your parents are often the first targets of your anger. 父母往往是你怒火最先针对的对象。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （要达成的）目标，指标（set/meet a target）
uncommonMeanings.example: We set a target of reading twelve novels this term. 我们定下本学期读十二本小说的目标。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 靶子，标靶（射击、射箭练习用）
uncommonMeanings.example: She fixed her eyes on the distant target. 她盯住远处的靶子。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 把……作为目标；瞄准，针对（target the root causes）
uncommonMeanings.example: An effective policy should target the root causes of stress. 有效的政策应针对压力的根源。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （把产品、广告等）面向，针对（特定人群，熟词僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: The campaign was targeted at teenagers who love phones. 这场活动面向爱玩手机的青少年。

posExamples.sentence: Whenever the pressure at school grew unbearable, my little brother became the easy target of my temper, and the sight of his trembling lip afterwards filled me with a shame I could not shake off. （读后续写·家庭亲情·愧疚）
I am writing to propose that our class set a realistic target of reading twelve English novels this term, so that every one of us can measure our progress and stay motivated. （应用文·建议信）
Rather than blaming individual students, an effective policy should target the root causes of academic stress, such as excessive homework and unrealistic parental expectations. （议论文·教育减负）
Steadying her breath, she fixed her eyes on the distant target, drew back the bowstring until her arm quivered, and let the arrow fly straight into the golden centre. （读后续写·射箭比赛·夺冠）

wordForms.other: 构词/拼写：target 作动词过去式、现在分词均不双写 t——targeted / targeting（重音在前音节 TAR-get，故不双写）。派生 targeted(adj.有针对性的)。搭配区分：a target FOR attack（攻击的对象）｜ a target OF criticism（批评的对象）｜ set/meet a target（指标）｜ on/off target（切中/偏离）。

idioms.translation: （预测、行动等）准确切中要害 / 偏离目标
idioms.example: Her guess about the surprise party was right on target, and she pretended to be astonished so as not to spoil her friends' careful planning. （读后续写·友谊·善意）

collocations.translation: 【课件】……的对象/靶子（of后接情绪/名词，如批评；for后接攻击行为/施动者）
collocations.example: Due to his improper comments on the Internet, Tom has become a target of criticism. 由于在网上的不当言论，汤姆成了众矢之的（批评的对象）。（课件原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】击中/未击中目标（靶子义）
collocations.example: Her first arrow missed the target, but the second hit it dead centre. 她第一箭脱靶，第二箭正中靶心。（课件搭配）

collocations.phrase: set / aim for / achieve / reach a target
collocations.translation: 【课件】设定/瞄准/达成/实现目标（指标义）
collocations.example: The team set a target and worked hard to reach it before the deadline. 团队定下目标，努力在截止前实现。（课件搭配）
We chose bright colours to appeal to our target audience. 我们选用亮色以吸引目标观众。（课件搭配）

collocations.translation: 【课件】如期，按目标（进展/预测切中）
collocations.example: The new stadium is on target to open in June. 新体育馆有望如期在六月开放。（课件原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】针对，面向（常用被动，target sth at/on sb）
collocations.example: The advertisement is mainly targeted at teenagers. 该广告主要针对青少年。（课件原句）
The company has targeted adults as its primary customers. 该公司将成年人作为其主要客户。（课件原句）

collocations.phrase: the first target(s) of one's anger
collocations.translation: 怒火最先针对的对象（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your anger. 当一切压力过大时，父母往往是你怒火最先针对的对象。（课文原句）

collocations.translation: ……的对象/靶子（for后接攻击行为，of后接情绪/名词）
collocations.example: He became an easy target for the bullies. 他成了恶霸们轻易下手的对象。
The coach encouraged each runner to set a personal target. 教练鼓励每位跑者设定个人目标。
The pupils finally met their fundraising target. 学生们终于达成了募款目标。

collocations.translation: 击中/未击中目标（靶子义）
collocations.example: His fourth arrow struck the target dead centre. 他的第四支箭正中靶心。
The quiet new boy quickly became an easy target. 那个安静的新生很快成了被欺负的对象。

collocations.translation: 目标受众/市场（v./attrib. 面向义）
collocations.example: We chose bright colours to appeal to our target audience. 我们选用亮色以吸引目标受众。
The reform became the target of fierce criticism. 这项改革成了猛烈批评的对象。

collocations.translation: 移动的靶子；不断变化的目标
collocations.example: Chasing perfection is like aiming at a moving target: the closer you get, the further the standard seems to retreat. （议论文·完美主义）
The volunteer scheme specifically targets left-behind children in rural areas, offering them weekly online lessons. （应用文·招募信）

synonyms.example: Keeping her ultimate goal firmly in mind, she refused to be discouraged. 心中牢牢记着终极目标，她拒绝气馁。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：goal 指长期追求的目的、抱负，偏抽象、偏理想；target 更具体、可量化、常有截止期限。句法：achieve/reach a goal；set/meet a target。

synonyms.example: The aim of this sale is to nurture responsibility in every participant. 义卖的目的是培养每位参与者的责任感。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：aim 指行动背后的意图或方向，语气正式、常单数；target 强调可衡量的具体指标。句法：the aim of doing / aim to do。

synonyms.example: Our first objective is to survey the neighbourhood. 我们的首要目标是调查社区。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：objective 书面、正式，常用于计划或商业语境，指分步骤要达成的明确任务；target 更侧重数字化指标。句法：achieve an objective。

synonyms.example: She had always been the victim of cruel jokes. 她一直是残忍玩笑的受害者。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：victim 特指受伤害、被针对的人，强调已受到的伤害；target 指被瞄准/攻击的对象，未必已受伤害。句法：the victim of sth / a target for sth。

advancedExpressions.expression: the target of anger/criticism（怒火/批评的对象）｜ a target for attack（攻击对象）｜ set/meet/achieve a target（设定/达成目标）｜ hit/miss the target（中/脱靶）｜ on/off target（切中/偏离）｜ target audience（目标受众）
advancedExpressions.example: 同一 target，介词 for/of 与搭配决定它是"靶子/对象"还是"指标"，成组记忆最省力。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能：表"目标/努力方向"（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: target ｜ goal ｜ aim ｜ objective
advancedExpressions.example: 写"设定并实现目标"可替换升级：set a target/goal → work towards our objective and finally achieve it（target 最可量化）。

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. became the target of ..., yet ...
advancedExpressions.example: Time and again my mother became the target of my thoughtless words, yet never once did the warmth in her eyes waver. （对比+never倒装，续写中反衬亲情的无私）

advancedExpressions.expression: with a clear target in mind, we can ...
advancedExpressions.example: With a clear target in mind — planting one thousand trees before spring — we can turn a vague wish into a measurable mission. （破折号补充说明，倡议信中把口号化为行动）

advancedExpressions.expression: instead of treating ... as a target, we ought to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Instead of treating struggling students as a target for blame, we ought to see them as individuals crying out for support. （instead of 对比结构，先破后立）

sentenceUpgrade.original: My brother was often the target of my anger.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Whenever the world outside pressed too hard upon me, it was my innocent little brother who bore the brunt of my anger — the nearest, gentlest target for a storm that was never really his to weather. （读后续写·心理描写+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Whenever 状语从句制造情境 + bear the brunt of 高级搭配 + 破折号补语 + storm 比喻愤怒 + 定语从句收尾

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should set a target and work hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm belief that once we set ourselves a clear and attainable target, and pursue it with unwavering determination, no obstacle will prove insurmountable. （应用文/议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm belief that 正式主句 + once 引导条件状语 + with unwavering determination 状语 + no ... insurmountable 否定强调

classPractice.type: 翻译句子（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: 知名演员通常是报纸、杂志报道的对象。（用 target of）
classPractice.answer: Well-known performers are usually targets of newspapers and magazines.
classPractice.note: 【课件】target(s) of sth=……的对象；performers为复数，target用复数targets。

classPractice.type: 翻译句子（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: 我们希望在战争中孩子们不要成为被攻击的目标。（用 be targeted）
classPractice.answer: We hope that children will not be targeted during the war.
classPractice.note: 【课件】be targeted=被作为攻击目标（=become targets）；此处用被动语态。

classPractice.type: 完成句子（课件·语境应用）
classPractice.question: 由于在网上的不当言论，汤姆成了众矢之的。Due to his improper comments on the Internet, Tom has become ____ ____ ____ ____ (众矢之的).
classPractice.note: 【课件】a target of criticism=批评的对象/众矢之的；批评义搭配用 of。

classPractice.question: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first ____ (target) of your anger.
classPractice.note: 还原课文原句：the first targets of your anger；parents 复数，target 用复数名词。

classPractice.question: The quiet new boy quickly became an easy target ____ the bullies by the gate. (for / of / to)
classPractice.note: a target for sb=某人（攻击/欺负）的对象，for 后接施动者；the target of criticism 用 of。

classPractice.question: 把"我建议全班设定本学期读十二本英语小说的目标"译成英文（用 set a target）。
classPractice.answer: I suggest (that) our class (should) set a target of reading twelve English novels this term.
classPractice.note: set a target of doing sth=设定做某事的目标；suggest 后从句用(should)+动词原形。

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your anger.
readingExamples: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your anger.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the strong feeling that you get when something has happened that you think is bad or unfair
(2) n. a state of being angry, often accompanied by a desire to hurt or blame others
(3) vt. (formal) to make someone feel angry

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 怒气，怒火（不可数，课文本义，targets of your anger）
uncommonMeanings.example: Your parents are often the first targets of your anger. 父母往往是你怒火最先针对的对象。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （正式）激怒，使发怒（高考熟词僻义，多用 It angered sb to ...）
uncommonMeanings.example: What angered the villagers most was the officials' cold indifference. 最激怒村民的是官员们冷漠的态度。

posExamples.sentence: The moment I saw my diary lying open on the desk, a wave of anger surged through me, hot and blinding, and before I could stop myself the harsh words had already left my mouth. （读后续写·家庭冲突·冲动）
I am writing to express, though not in anger, my deep concern about the recent decision to shorten our lunch break, which I believe deserves careful reconsideration. （应用文·投诉/建议信）
Anger, if left unchecked, clouds our judgement and turns small misunderstandings into lasting wounds; learning to master it is therefore an essential part of growing up. （议论文·情绪管理）
It angered her to see how quickly her sacrifice had been forgotten, yet she chose silence over a quarrel that would heal nothing. （读后续写·委屈·克制）

wordForms.other: 词族全家桶：anger(n./v.)-angry(adj.)-angrily(adv.)。拼写贴士：angry 变副词去 y 加 ily→angrily。搭配区分：be angry WITH/AT sb（对某人生气）｜ be angry ABOUT/AT sth（为某事生气）。anger 作名词通常不可数（无复数），短语 in anger / a fit of anger。

idioms.example: In a fit of anger he slammed the door, only to spend the whole night regretting the pain he had caused his mother. （读后续写·冲动后悔）

collocations.phrase: the first target(s) of one's anger
collocations.translation: 怒火最先针对的对象（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your anger. 当一切压力过大时，父母往往是你怒火最先针对的对象。（课文原句）
Never make an important promise in anger. 千万别在气头上作重要承诺。
She struggled to control her anger and stayed polite. 她努力克制怒火，保持礼貌。
Rather than venting his anger on teammates, he channelled it into the sprint. 他没有把火撒在队友身上，而是化作冲刺的力量。
A sudden surge of anger rose in my chest. 一股怒火忽然涌上我的胸口。
He almost burst with anger at the unfair comment. 那条不公的评论让他几乎怒火中烧。
The referee's mistake provoked anger among the fans. 裁判的失误激起了球迷的愤怒。
For the sake of peace, he swallowed his anger. 为了息事宁人，他忍气吞声。
Seething with anger yet forcing a polite smile, she thanked the judges and walked off the stage with her head held high. （读后续写·比赛失利·尊严）

synonyms.example: Blind with rage, he hurled the trophy across the room. 他怒不可遏，把奖杯扔到房间另一头。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：rage 语气最强，指几近失控的暴怒；anger 是较中性、程度更广的怒气。句法：in a rage / blind with rage，多不可数。

synonyms.example: Her eyes blazed with a quiet fury. 她双眼燃着一种无声的盛怒。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：fury 强调猛烈而外露的愤怒，文学色彩浓，常与暴风雨意象搭配；anger 更日常。句法：in a fury / with fury。

synonyms.example: Years of being overlooked bred deep resentment in her. 长年被忽视让她心生深深怨恨。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：resentment 指因不公而长期郁积的怨恨，偏内向、持久；anger 常是即时爆发的情绪。句法：resentment at/towards sb。

synonyms.example: A flicker of irritation crossed his face. 他脸上闪过一丝恼怒。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：irritation 程度最轻，指因小事而生的短暂恼火；anger 程度更重、更持久。句法：in irritation / a flicker of irritation。

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·anger 情绪表达族
advancedExpressions.expression: in anger（气头上）｜ in a fit of anger（一时气愤下）｜ a wave/surge of anger（一阵怒火）｜ control/swallow one's anger（克制/忍住怒火）｜ vent one's anger（发泄）｜ boil/burst with anger（怒火中烧）
advancedExpressions.example: 从"起怒—忍怒—泄怒"一整条链，读后续写情绪描写可成组调用。

advancedExpressions.type: 构词法·anger 词族与主谓/搭配
advancedExpressions.expression: anger(n./v.) → angry(adj.) → angrily(adv.)；be angry with sb / about sth
advancedExpressions.example: It angered me（v.激怒）；I was angry with him（adj.生某人的气）；she replied angrily（adv.）——同根三词，词性到位。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能：表"愤怒"（按强度可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: irritation（轻）＜ anger（一般）＜ fury / rage（强）；resentment（积怨）
advancedExpressions.example: 写作按强度选词：a flicker of irritation → a wave of anger → blind with rage，程度递进更精准。

advancedExpressions.expression: a wave of anger surged through sb., only to ...
advancedExpressions.example: A wave of anger surged through me, only to melt away the instant I noticed the tears welling in her eyes. （only to 引出意外转折，愤怒瞬间被亲情化解）

advancedExpressions.expression: not in anger but out of concern, I ...
advancedExpressions.example: Not in anger but out of concern, I feel obliged to point out a few problems with the current arrangement. （not ... but ... 对比，投诉信中先声明善意立场）

advancedExpressions.expression: anger, once mastered, can be transformed into ...
advancedExpressions.example: Anger, once mastered, can be transformed into a powerful force for change rather than a source of regret. （插入语 once mastered + rather than 对比，辩证看待情绪）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I was very angry and shouted at my mother.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Anger flared up inside me like a struck match, and before reason could intervene, I had already flung those cruel words at the one person who loved me most — my mother. （读后续写·心理+比喻+悔恨）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: flare up like a struck match 明喻愤怒 + before reason could intervene 状语强调冲动 + 破折号点题(母亲) + fling 强动词

sentenceUpgrade.original: The unfair decision made many people angry.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The manifestly unfair decision stirred widespread anger, giving voice to a discontent that had long been simmering beneath the surface. （议论文·社会·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: manifestly 副词加强 + stir anger 高级搭配 + giving voice to 分词状语 + simmer beneath the surface 比喻积怨

classPractice.question: When it all gets too much, your parents are often the first targets of your ____ (angry).
classPractice.note: 还原课文原句：of your anger；此处需名词，angry 是形容词，改用名词 anger。

classPractice.question: 用 anger/angry/angrily 填空并变形："How could you read my diary?" she shouted ____, tears springing to her eyes.
classPractice.note: 修饰动词 shouted 需副词 angrily；注意 angry 去 y 加 ily 的拼写。

classPractice.question: ____ ____ ____ ____ ____, he slammed the door, only to regret it all night. (一时气愤之下)
classPractice.note: in a fit of anger=一时气愤之下，固定短语；anger 作名词不可数。

sub_section: Pre-reading
original_sentence: What physical and mental changes do you experience as you become a teenager?
readingExamples: What physical and mental changes do you experience as you become a teenager?
definitionEn:
(1) adj. relating to the mind, or involving the process of thinking
(2) adj. relating to illnesses or conditions of the mind
(3) adj. done in the mind, without speaking or writing
(4) adj. (informal, BrE) crazy or extremely foolish

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①（与心智、思维有关的）精神的，智力的（mental changes 心理变化；mental ability 智力）
uncommonMeanings.example: The job demands great mental effort rather than physical strength. 这份工作需要的是脑力而非体力。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②（与心理疾病有关的）精神的（mental health 心理健康；mental illness 精神疾病）
uncommonMeanings.example: More schools now offer support for students' mental health. 越来越多学校为学生提供心理健康支持。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③在心里进行的，不落笔的（如心算）（熟词僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Without a calculator, the old shopkeeper did a quick mental sum and handed back the exact change. （读后续写·人物·细节·熟词僻义）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ④（英式口语）疯狂的，荒唐的（熟词僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: "You want to swim across the lake in November? That's absolutely mental!" she cried, half amused and half horrified. （读后续写·对话·熟词僻义）

posExamples.sentence: As the exam drew nearer, I felt not only physically exhausted but mentally drained, as though every thought had to be dragged out of a fog. （读后续写·备考·压力）
I am writing to suggest that our school open a counselling room, for the mental health of students deserves as much attention as their academic results. （应用文·建议信）
True education should nurture not merely physical strength but mental resilience — the quiet courage to rise again after every failure. （议论文·教育本质）
Closing her eyes, the diver made a swift mental note of every movement she had rehearsed, then stepped calmly onto the edge of the board. （读后续写·比赛·专注）

wordForms.other: 反义/对照词 physical (身体的)；派生 mentally 副词位于系动词后或过去分词前 (mentally drained/prepared)；注意 mental 无比较级，程度用 highly/purely mental 修饰；易错拼写：mentality 结尾 -ality 双 l 只一个

idioms.example: She made a mental note to thank the stranger who had returned her lost wallet, though she never saw him again. （读后续写·善意·遗憾）

collocations.translation: 身体和心理的变化（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: What physical and mental changes do you experience as you become a teenager? 当你步入青春期时，你会经历哪些身体和心理上的变化？
Regular exercise benefits our mental health. 规律锻炼有益心理健康。
The teenage years bring both mental and physical changes. 青春期带来身心两方面的变化。
What set the champion apart was sheer mental strength. 让冠军脱颖而出的正是过硬的心理素质。
She made a mental note to thank him later. 她暗自记下稍后要谢他。
After the exam I was mentally drained. 考完试我心力交瘁。
A positive mental attitude makes learning easier. 积极的心态让学习更轻松。
For years she carried a vivid mental picture of that snowy morning when her grandfather taught her to skate. （读后续写·回忆·温情）
The competition tested the pupils' mental arithmetic, and hands shot up before the teacher had even finished the question. （读后续写·课堂）
To relieve the mental pressure of the final term, our class organized a weekly hiking trip. （应用文·活动通知）

synonyms.example: The boy's fear of exams was largely psychological. 那男孩的考试恐惧多半是心理层面的。
synonyms.usage: 更学术、强调深层心理机制，多用于正式或专业语境，常修饰 problem/support；mental 更日常、覆盖面更广，常搭 health/state

synonyms.translation: 身体的，物质的（反义辨析）
synonyms.example: Growing up brings both physical and mental changes. 成长既带来身体也带来心理的变化。
synonyms.usage: physical 指身体/物质层面，常与 mental 并置对照（physical and mental）；mental 指心智/精神层面，二者句法位置相同，作定语修饰同类名词

synonyms.example: Chess demands intense intellectual concentration rather than physical effort. （议论文·智力活动）
synonyms.usage: 特指与理性、知识、思考能力相关；mental 还可指情绪与精神状态，范围更宽

synonyms.example: Facing the empty seat at the dinner table, she needed emotional support far more than any advice. （读后续写·失落）
synonyms.usage: 侧重情感层面；mental 偏思维/精神层面，二者常并列使用(mental and emotional)

advancedExpressions.expression: mental health / mental strength / mental note / mental arithmetic / physical and mental
advancedExpressions.example: 同一 mental 拉出一串搭配：mental health 心理健康、mental strength 意志力、make a mental note 暗自记下、mental arithmetic 心算、physical and mental 身心的。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（"心理/精神层面"，只枚举可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: mental / psychological / emotional / inner
advancedExpressions.example: 描述内在层面可替换：mental well-being ≈ psychological well-being ≈ emotional well-being ≈ inner well-being（越靠后越偏情感/内心）。

advancedExpressions.expression: mental (adj.) → mentally (adv.) → mentality (n.)
advancedExpressions.example: 形容词加 -ly 变副词 mentally，加 -ity 变名词 mentality，词根 ment- 表"心智"（对照 mention/comment 同源）。

advancedExpressions.expression: physically ... yet mentally ...
advancedExpressions.example: Physically drained yet mentally alert, she forced her trembling legs up the final flight of stairs. （yet 转折并置身心状态，强化坚持的张力）

advancedExpressions.expression: the mental ... of ... deserves no less attention than ...
advancedExpressions.example: The mental well-being of every student deserves no less attention than their examination scores. （no less ... than 比较结构，建议信中强调重视心理健康）

advancedExpressions.expression: not merely physical ... but also mental ...
advancedExpressions.example: Genuine strength lies not merely in physical endurance but also in mental resilience. （not merely ... but also ... 递进，辩证界定何为强大）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The exam made me very tired in my mind.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: By the time the last bell rang, I was mentally drained, my mind as heavy and slow as a machine that had been running far too long without rest. （读后续写·心理描写+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: By the time 时间状语从句 + mentally drained 精准搭配 + as ... as a machine 明喻疲惫 + running without rest 补充意象

sentenceUpgrade.original: Students' mental health is important.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It cannot be overemphasized that a student's mental health forms the very foundation upon which lasting academic success is built. （议论文/应用文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It cannot be overemphasized that 正式强调句 + form the foundation 比喻 + upon which 定语从句 + the very 加强语气

classPractice.question: 当你步入青春期时，你会经历哪些身体和心理上的变化？What ____ and ____ changes do you experience as you become a teenager?
classPractice.note: 课文原句；physical and mental 身心的，常并置作定语

classPractice.question: Our teacher reminded us that regular exercise benefits not only the body but also our ____ (mental) health.
classPractice.note: 此处修饰名词 health 需用形容词原形 mental，不是副词 mentally

classPractice.question: After three sleepless nights of revision, she felt physically fine but ____ (mental / mentally) exhausted.
classPractice.note: 修饰形容词 exhausted 须用副词 mentally；与 physically 对照

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: You enter a strange middle ground – you are no longer a small child but not quite an adult.
readingExamples: You enter a strange middle ground – you are no longer a small child but not quite an adult.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a fully grown person who is legally responsible for their actions
(2) n. a fully grown animal
(3) adj. having grown to full size and strength; typical of or suitable for grown-up people
(4) adj. mature and sensible in behaviour

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①成年人（法律上对自己行为负责的成年人）
uncommonMeanings.example: You are no longer a small child but not quite an adult. 你不再是小孩子，但又还算不上成年人。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②（动物的）成年个体，成体
uncommonMeanings.example: The tiny cub had grown into a magnificent adult. 那只小幼崽已长成一头威武的成年野兽。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③成年的；适合成人的，成人（尺寸/内容）的（an adult ticket 成人票）
uncommonMeanings.example: This film contains adult themes and is not suitable for children. 这部影片含成人题材，不适合儿童。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ④成熟稳重的，有担当的（熟词僻义，形容行为、态度）
uncommonMeanings.example: He handled the disappointment in a remarkably adult way, thanking his rivals and quietly vowing to try again. （读后续写·成长·成熟·熟词僻义）

posExamples.sentence: Standing at the school gate for the first time without my mother's hand to hold, I suddenly felt the weight of becoming an adult pressing gently upon my shoulders. （读后续写·成长·独立）
I am writing to invite adults from our community to join the reading programme, so that young and old alike can share the joy of good books. （应用文·邀请信）
The teenage years are a strange in-between stage: no longer a carefree child, yet not quite ready for the full adult responsibilities that lie ahead. （议论文·青春期成长）
The tiny cub that had once fit in my palm was now a magnificent adult, and watching it stride into the forest, I felt both proud and heartbroken. （读后续写·动物·离别）

wordForms.adjective: adult (成年的) / grown-up (成年的，口语)
wordForms.other: adulting (成年人的日常责任，非正式)；名词短语 reach/enter adulthood 步入成年；构词 adult + -hood(表状态/时期) = adulthood，同类 childhood/neighbourhood；美式重音 /əˈdʌlt/，英式 /ˈædʌlt/

collocations.translation: 还算不上成年人（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: You are no longer a small child but not quite an adult. 你不再是小孩子，但又还算不上成年人。
The shy girl had grown into a confident young adult. 那个害羞的女孩已长成自信的青年。
As a young adult, she was eager to prove herself. 作为一个青年，她渴望证明自己。
Only when we reach adulthood do we understand our parents. 直到成年我们才懂父母。
A summer job gave me a first taste of adult responsibilities. 暑期工让我初尝成年人的责任。
All I wanted was for my parents to treat me like an adult. 我只希望父母把我当成年人看待。
The exhibition was designed to delight adults and children alike. （应用文·活动介绍）

collocations.phrase: act like an adult / in an adult manner
collocations.example: He surprised everyone by acting like an adult, calmly settling the quarrel his classmates had started. （读后续写·成熟）

synonyms.example: "When I'm a grown-up, I'll build a house full of roses." “等我长大，我要盖一座开满玫瑰的房子。”
synonyms.usage: 口语化、亲切，多见于对话或儿童语境，可作名词(a grown-up)或形容词(grown-up children)；adult 更中性、正式，可用于书面与法律文本，二者句法位置一致

synonyms.example: Her calm response to the crisis proved how mature she had become. （读后续写·成长）
synonyms.usage: 形容词，强调心智/情感的成熟；adult 作形容词可指成熟，但更常指'成年的'这一年龄属性

synonyms.example: The frightened boy who had run away years ago returned as a grave and silent man. （读后续写·蜕变）
synonyms.usage: 具体指成年男女，带性别；adult 不分性别，是更概括、更中性的说法

advancedExpressions.expression: become an adult / reach adulthood / grow into a young adult / adult responsibilities
advancedExpressions.example: "长大成人"一串说法：become an adult、grow into a young adult、reach/enter adulthood、shoulder adult responsibilities。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（"成年人"，只枚举可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: adult / grown-up / man·woman / a person of full age
advancedExpressions.example: 指成年人可替换：an adult ≈ a grown-up ≈ a man/woman（带性别）≈ a person of full age（正式/法律）。

advancedExpressions.expression: adult (n./adj.) → adulthood (n.)
advancedExpressions.example: 加后缀 -hood 表"时期/状态"：adult→adulthood 成年期，childhood 童年，parenthood 为人父母。

advancedExpressions.expression: no longer ..., yet not quite ..., sb. stood at ...
advancedExpressions.example: No longer a child, yet not quite an adult, I stood at the threshold of a life I did not yet know how to live. （no longer ... yet not quite ... 对照，捕捉青春期的迷惘）

advancedExpressions.expression: we warmly invite adults and youngsters alike to ...
advancedExpressions.example: We warmly invite adults and youngsters alike to take part in this community clean-up. （... and ... alike 涵盖各年龄，邀请信中扩大参与感）

advancedExpressions.expression: becoming an adult means not ... but ...
advancedExpressions.example: Becoming an adult means not the freedom to do whatever we please, but the wisdom to shoulder what we must. （not ... but ... 对比重新定义成年，先破后立）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I am not a child but not an adult yet.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I found myself trapped in a strange middle ground — no longer the child who cried for sweets, yet not yet the adult who could stand unshaken against the storms of life. （读后续写·成长·比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: trapped in a middle ground 意象 + 破折号补充 + no longer ... yet not yet 平行对照 + storms of life 比喻人生困境 + 两个定语从句丰满形象

sentenceUpgrade.original: When we grow up, we understand our parents.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is often not until we ourselves step into adulthood that we come to grasp the depth of the love our parents so quietly gave. （议论文/读后续写·感恩·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is not until ... that 强调句 + step into adulthood 高级搭配 + come to grasp 渐悟 + so quietly gave 副词点出无声的付出

classPractice.question: 你不再是小孩子，但又还算不上成年人。You are no longer a small child but not quite ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；not quite an adult 还算不上成年人，adult 前用不定冠词 an

classPractice.question: Only when we reach ____ (adult) do we begin to understand our parents' sacrifices.
classPractice.note: reach 后接名词 adulthood(成年)；此处需名词而非形容词 adult

classPractice.question: In the fairy tale, the child says: "When I'm a ____ (adult / grown-up), I'll travel the world."
classPractice.note: 对话/童真语境两者皆可，grown-up 更口语亲切；书面正式首选 adult

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: You have a strong desire for independence and you want to be trusted.
readingExamples: You have a strong desire for independence and you want to be trusted.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a strong feeling of wanting to have something or wishing for something to happen
(2) n. a strong wish to have sex with someone
(3) vt. (formal) to want something, especially strongly
(4) vt. (formal) to ask for or request something in a polite, formal way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①渴望，欲望（强烈想拥有或希望发生的感觉）（a desire for sth；a desire to do sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: You have a strong desire for independence. 你对独立有强烈的渴望。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②（正式）（强烈地）想要，渴望（desire sth / desire to do sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: Human beings have always desired freedom. 人类始终渴望自由。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③（正式）请求，要求（常用于告示、书面语，多用被动 sb is desired to do）（熟词僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: Passengers are desired to remain seated until the aircraft has come to a complete stop. （应用文·正式告示·熟词僻义）

posExamples.sentence: Beneath my quiet exterior burned a fierce desire to prove that a country girl from a mountain village could win a place at the very best university. （读后续写·励志·内心）
I am writing to express my strong desire to join the school's environmental club, whose recent tree-planting campaign moved me deeply. （应用文·申请信）
History shows that human beings have always desired freedom, and no wall, however high, can imprison that longing forever. （议论文·自由·论证）
As a teenager, you feel a growing desire for independence, a longing to be trusted and to make your own choices at last. （读后续写/议论文·青春期）

wordForms.adjective: desirable (值得拥有的，可取的) / desirous (formal 渴望的) / undesirable (不受欢迎的，反义)
wordForms.other: desire 名词、动词同形；结构 a desire for + n. / a desire to do；注意 desirable 表"值得要的"(客观)，desirous 表"渴望的"(主观，接 of doing)；易混：leave much to be desired = 不尽人意（固定被动结构）

idioms.example: Although the plan was ambitious, its execution left much to be desired, and the event ended in chaos. （议论文/应用文·评价·委婉批评）
She had finally won her heart's desire — a scholarship to study abroad — yet the joy was tinged with the ache of leaving home. （读后续写·梦想成真·五味杂陈）

collocations.translation: 【课件】对……的渴望（n. a strong hope/wish）
collocations.example: You have both a new desire for independence and a continued need to be looked after. 你既有对独立的新渴望，又持续需要被照顾。

collocations.phrase: a strong / no desire to do sth
collocations.translation: 【课件】做某事的强烈欲望 / 无意做某事
collocations.example: Due to the air pollution, there is a growing desire for clean energy among city dwellers. 因为空气污染，城市居民对于清洁能源的渴望日益增强。

collocations.phrase: express a desire to do sth
collocations.example: He expressed a desire to see his hometown again. 他表达了想再看看家乡的愿望。
Nothing could satisfy her desire for knowledge. 没有什么能满足她对知识的渴望。
The girl desired to go back to her motherland. 这个女孩渴望回国。
Tom told me that they desired me to return soon. 汤姆告诉我他们要我快点回来。

collocations.translation: 【课件】(vt.) 渴望……（从句用虚拟 should + 动词原形）
collocations.example: The girl desired that she (should) go back to her motherland. 这个女孩渴望回国。
It has been 3 months since he left home, and now he is desirous of finding a job to support himself. 离家已经3个月了，现在他渴望找到一份工作来养活自己。

collocations.translation: 【课件】(adj. desired) 预期的效果 / 结果
collocations.example: It failed to create the desired effect. 没有达到预期的效果。

collocations.translation: 【课件】(adj. desirable) ……是可取的 / 明智的（值得做的，从句常用虚拟 should）
collocations.example: It is desirable that several tests should be carried out before the product is launched. 在产品上市前进行几次试验是可取的做法。

collocations.translation: 对独立的强烈渴望（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: You have a strong desire for independence and you want to be trusted. 你渴望独立，也希望被信任。
She felt a sudden desire to apologize. 她突然很想道歉。
A burning desire to make his mother proud kept him going. 想让母亲骄傲的强烈渴望支撑着他。

collocations.phrase: have no desire to do sth
collocations.example: I have no desire to win at the cost of a friendship. 我不愿以友情为代价去赢。

collocations.translation: 很不理想，有待改进（熟词僻义结构）
collocations.example: The plan was bold, but its execution left much to be desired. 计划很大胆，执行却不尽人意。
Volunteering at the shelter finally fulfilled her lifelong desire to make a real difference. （读后续写·公益·圆满）
In his letter he expressed a heartfelt desire to see his hometown transformed by education. （应用文·书信）

collocations.phrase: resist the desire to do sth
collocations.example: She had to resist the desire to peek at the answers, reminding herself that honesty mattered more than marks. （读后续写·诚信·挣扎）

synonyms.translation: 【课件】渴望的（adj. 主观，接 of doing/sth）
synonyms.example: Now he is desirous of finding a job to support himself. = he is longing for a job / he desires a job / he has a strong desire to find a job. 现在他渴望找到一份工作养活自己。
synonyms.usage: 【课件】desirous 为 desire 的形容词，主观强调"渴望的"，固定搭 be desirous of (doing) sth，等价于 be longing for / have a strong desire to do；区别于 desirable(客观"值得要的")

synonyms.translation: 【课件】可取的，明智的，值得拥有的（adj. 客观）
synonyms.example: It is desirable that several tests should be carried out before the product is launched. 在产品上市前进行几次试验是可取的做法。
synonyms.usage: 【课件】= advisable / attractive，客观评价"值得做/值得拥有"；It is desirable that... 从句常用虚拟 (should) do；与主观的 desirous 相区别

synonyms.example: She made a silent wish for her grandmother to get well. 她默默许愿祖母康复。
synonyms.usage: 语气温和，指一般愿望，常搭 make a wish/wish for sth，也可作动词 wish to do；desire 程度更强、更迫切，名词常搭 a strong/burning desire for

synonyms.example: A quiet longing for home washed over her as she watched the autumn leaves drift past the classroom window. （读后续写·思乡·细腻）
synonyms.usage: 偏文学、偏情感，常含思念、向往的绵长意味，多作名词 a longing for/to do；desire 更直接、更有目标性

synonyms.example: Her greatest aspiration was to open a free library in every village. （议论文/应用文·理想）
synonyms.usage: 指崇高、长远的理想抱负，褒义且正式，常搭 career/lifelong aspiration；desire 覆盖面更广，可大可小

synonyms.example: After months in the wilderness, he was seized by an overwhelming craving for home. （读后续写·渴求）
synonyms.usage: 指几乎难以抑制的强烈渴求，常带本能、身体层面色彩，搭 a craving for；desire 更理性、更宽泛

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·desire 家族三形容词辨析（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: desired（预期的）/ desirable（可取的，客观）/ desirous（渴望的，主观 of）
advancedExpressions.example: 【课件】the desired result 预期的结果；It is desirable that tests (should) be carried out 做试验是可取的；he is desirous of finding a job 他渴望找到工作。三词同源不同义，考点常放一处三选。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·desire 接从句用虚拟语气（课件）
advancedExpressions.expression: desire that + 主语 + (should) + 动词原形
advancedExpressions.example: 【课件】The girl desired that she (should) go back to her motherland. 同类 It is desirable that ... (should) do。desire/desirable 后 that 从句谓语用 (should) do。

advancedExpressions.expression: a desire for sth / a desire to do / a burning desire / have no desire to do / leave much to be desired
advancedExpressions.example: 同一 desire 拉出一串：a strong desire for independence、a desire to apologize、a burning desire、have no desire to argue、leave much to be desired。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（"渴望"，只枚举可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: desire / wish / longing / craving / yearning
advancedExpressions.example: "渴望做某事"可替换：a desire to do ≈ a wish to do ≈ a longing to do ≈ a yearning to do（后二者更文学、更绵长）。

advancedExpressions.expression: desire (n./v.) → desirable (adj.) → desirably (adv.) / desirous (adj.)
advancedExpressions.example: 加 -able 表"可…的"→desirable 合意的；加否定前缀 un- →undesirable 不受欢迎的；词根 -sire 表"渴望"。

advancedExpressions.expression: beneath ..., there burned a desire to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Beneath her shy silence there burned a fierce desire to be seen, to be heard, to matter. （倒装 there burned + 三个不定式排比，层层揭示隐藏的渴望）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is my sincere desire to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is my sincere desire to contribute my modest efforts to this meaningful cause. （It is my sincere desire to ... 正式句式，申请信中表明诚意）

advancedExpressions.expression: the desire for ... is what drives ...
advancedExpressions.example: The desire for a better life is what drives ordinary people to accomplish extraordinary things. （the ... is what drives ... 强调结构，揭示动机与成就的因果）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She really wanted to be independent.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Within her stirred a restless desire for independence — a quiet but insistent voice urging her to step out from her parents' shadow and find a path she could truly call her own. （读后续写·心理描写+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Within her stirred 倒装 + restless desire 形容词精准 + 破折号补充 + a voice 拟人化欲望 + step out from ... shadow 比喻 + 定语从句收束

sentenceUpgrade.original: Everyone wants to be free.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The desire for freedom, deeply rooted in the human heart, has throughout history driven countless people to dream, to struggle, and to sacrifice. （议论文·自由·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: deeply rooted in ... 分词插入语 + throughout history 时间状语 + drive sb to do + to dream/struggle/sacrifice 三不定式排比递进

classPractice.type: 语法填空（课件·完成句子）
classPractice.question: Due to the air pollution, there is a growing ____ ____ clean energy among city dwellers. （因为空气污染，城市居民对于清洁能源的渴望日益增强。）
classPractice.note: 【课件】a desire for sth 对……的渴望，介词固定用 for

classPractice.type: 语法填空（课件·完成句子）

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: Just remember that it is completely normal to struggle with the stress that parent-child tensions create, and that you and your parents can work together to improve your relationship.
readingExamples: Just remember that it is completely normal to struggle with the stress that parent-child tensions create, and that you and your parents can work together to improve your relationship.
definitionEn:
(1) vi. to try very hard to do something difficult, or to fight against something
(2) vi. to fight or push violently against someone in order to get free
(3) vi. to move somewhere with great effort
(4) n. a long and difficult attempt to achieve something, or a fight

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①（努力克服困难）挣扎，奋斗，斗争（struggle to do / with / against / for）
uncommonMeanings.example: It is normal to struggle with the stress of adolescence. 为青春期的压力而挣扎是正常的。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②（为挣脱而）扭动，搏斗，反抗
uncommonMeanings.example: The frightened bird struggled in his hands. 受惊的小鸟在他手中拼命扑腾。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③（费力地）挪动，艰难前行（熟词僻义，常接 up/along/through）
uncommonMeanings.example: Weighed down by the enormous backpack, the exhausted hiker struggled up the last icy slope, one trembling step at a time. （读后续写·登山·坚持·熟词僻义）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ④（长期而艰难的）努力，奋斗；搏斗，斗争（a struggle for/against/to do）
uncommonMeanings.example: Learning to walk again was an uphill struggle. 重新学走路是一场艰难的苦战。

posExamples.sentence: For weeks I struggled to make sense of the equations, until one sleepless night everything suddenly fell into place like scattered stars forming a constellation. （读后续写·学习·顿悟）
I am writing to share how our team overcame the struggle of organizing the charity concert, in the hope that future volunteers may learn from our experience. （应用文·经验分享信）
It is completely normal to struggle with the pressures of adolescence; what matters is not that we fall, but that we choose to rise each time. （议论文·成长·励志）
Watching my grandfather's lifelong struggle against poverty, I came to understand that dignity is not given but earned through quiet perseverance. （读后续写·亲情·感悟）

wordForms.noun: struggle (奋斗，斗争) — 与动词同形
wordForms.other: 动词、名词同形；核心结构辨析：struggle to do(努力做某事) / struggle with sth(与…作斗争) / struggle against sth(抗争) / struggle for sth(争取)；固定短语 struggle to one's feet 挣扎起身；an uphill struggle 艰苦努力

idioms.example: In the frozen wilderness, every creature is locked in a relentless struggle for survival. （读后续写/议论文·自然·生存）
Learning to walk again after the accident was an uphill struggle, yet she met each painful day with a stubborn smile. （读后续写·康复·顽强）

collocations.translation: 【课件】努力做某事（try very hard to do sth）
collocations.example: They struggled just to pay their bills. 他们仅仅为了付账单就已经很吃力。Lance struggled to strike a balance between work and family. Lance 努力平衡工作和家庭的关系。
Chris struggled for breath. 克里斯艰难地喘着气。
Rachel struggled with her conscience and decided to tell the truth. 蕾切尔经过一番良心上的斗争，终于说了真相。
He struggled against cancer for two years. 他和癌症抗争了两年。
Students will continue their struggle for their ideal university in the next few years. 学生们在接下来几年里将继续为理想大学奋斗。
She never gives up her struggle against shyness. 她从未放弃过克服羞怯的斗争。Her struggle with the disease lasted ten years. 她与疾病的斗争持续了十年。
Your proposal seems rushed, so it will be a struggle to make them accept it. 你的提案显得仓促，让他们接受会是件难事。

collocations.translation: 为压力而苦苦挣扎（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: It is completely normal to struggle with the stress that parent-child tensions create. 为亲子矛盾带来的压力而挣扎是完全正常的。
The novel portrays a bitter power struggle. 这部小说描绘了激烈的权力斗争。
Bruised and breathless, the boxer struggled to his feet. 遍体鳞伤、气喘吁吁，那拳手挣扎着站了起来。
Trapped beneath the collapsed beam, the miner waged a silent life-and-death struggle until the rescuers' lights finally appeared. （读后续写·灾难·求生）

collocations.translation: 经过一番挣扎 / 努力之后
collocations.example: After much struggle, our class finally reached an agreement that satisfied everyone. （应用文·活动记叙）

synonyms.example: We should strive for excellence, not out of fear of failure, but out of love. 我们应追求卓越，不是出于对失败的恐惧，而是出于热爱。
synonyms.usage: 更正式、更积极，纯指'努力追求'，无'吃力/挣扎'负担感，常搭 strive for/to do；struggle 常含困难、痛苦，句法上 struggle to do / with sth

synonyms.example: For days he wrestled with the difficult decision. 他为那个艰难的抉择纠结了好几天。
synonyms.usage: 常指与抽象难题(问题、决定、良心)反复较量，画面感强，固定搭 wrestle with；struggle 适用范围更广，可接 with/against/for/to do

synonyms.example: She vowed to fight for her dream no matter what. 无论如何她都发誓为梦想而战。
synonyms.usage: 语气强烈直接，可指具体或抽象的战斗，搭 fight for/against；struggle 更强调持续吃力的过程

synonyms.example: For three long years she battled her illness with great courage. （读后续写·抗病·励志）
synonyms.usage: 强调长期、艰苦、需要勇气的对抗，常与疾病、逆境搭配(battle against/with)；比 struggle 更具英雄色彩

advancedExpressions.expression: struggle with / against / for / to do / struggle to one's feet / an uphill struggle
advancedExpressions.example: 一个 struggle 靠介词分工：struggle with sth 为…挣扎、struggle against sth 抗争、struggle for sth 争取、struggle to do 努力做、struggle to one's feet 挣扎起身。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（"努力/奋斗"，只枚举可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: struggle to do / strive to do / fight to do / battle to do / endeavour to do
advancedExpressions.example: "奋力做某事"可替换：struggle to do ≈ strive to do ≈ fight to do ≈ endeavour to do（越靠后越正式，struggle 最含吃力感）。

advancedExpressions.expression: struggle (v.) → struggle (n. 同形) → struggling (adj.)
advancedExpressions.example: 动词直接转作名词(a hard struggle)；加 -ing 作形容词 struggling 苦苦经营的(a struggling business)。

advancedExpressions.expression: it is not ... that defines us, but the struggle to ...
advancedExpressions.example: It is not how gracefully we win that defines us, but the struggle to rise every time we fall. （It is not ... that ..., but ... 强调对比，续写结尾点明成长真谛）

advancedExpressions.expression: through all the struggles, we came to realize that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Through all the struggles of preparing the exhibition, we came to realize that teamwork can turn the impossible into the achievable. （through 状语 + came to realize 渐悟，分享信中提炼收获）

advancedExpressions.expression: struggle is not the enemy of growth but its very ...
advancedExpressions.example: Struggle is not the enemy of growth but its very engine, forging character in the heat of hardship. （not ... but ... 重新定义 + engine/forge 比喻，论证挫折的价值）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He tried hard to climb the mountain.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Gasping for breath and clutching at frozen rocks, he struggled up the final slope, each step a silent battle between his failing strength and his unyielding will. （读后续写·登山·意志力）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 分词状语(Gasping..., clutching...)开头造画面 + struggle up 精准搭配 + each step a battle 隐喻 + failing strength vs unyielding will 对比升华

sentenceUpgrade.original: It is normal to have difficulties in life.

translation: 艰难的；粗糙的；不确切的
sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: On the other hand, when you are struggling to control your feelings, you wish they could be more caring and patient – sometimes they forget that growing up is a rough ride.
readingExamples: On the other hand, when you are struggling to control your feelings, you wish they could be more caring and patient – sometimes they forget that growing up is a rough ride.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. having an uneven surface; not smooth or level
(2) adj. difficult and full of problems; unpleasant to experience
(3) adj. not exact or detailed; approximate
(4) adj. (of the sea or weather) with strong wind or storms; violent

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①【课件】艰难的，不好受的（= difficult, hard；a rough ride/time）
uncommonMeanings.example: Growing up is a rough ride. He's had a really rough time recently. 成长是一段艰难的旅程；他最近过得很艰难。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②【课件】大致的，不确切的（not exact；a rough guess/idea）
uncommonMeanings.example: There were about 20 people there, at a rough guess. 粗略估计，那里大约有20人。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③【课件】粗糙的，不平的（not smooth；rough hands/skin）
uncommonMeanings.example: The skin on her hands was hard and rough. 她手上的皮肤又硬又粗糙。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ④【课件】繁重的（体力活）（the hard physical work；rough work）
uncommonMeanings.example: We'll get someone in to do the rough work. 我们会找人来干粗重的体力活。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①表面不平的，粗糙的（a rough surface；rough hands）
uncommonMeanings.example: The rough bark scratched her palm as she climbed. 她攀爬时粗糙的树皮划破了手心。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②艰难的，充满困难的，不好受的（a rough ride/time/patch）
uncommonMeanings.example: Growing up is a rough ride. 成长是一段颠簸艰难的旅程。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③不确切的，大致的，粗略的（a rough idea/estimate/draft）
uncommonMeanings.example: According to our rough estimate, over two hundred students would benefit. 据我们粗略估计，将有两百多名学生受益。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ④（海面、天气）波涛汹涌的，狂风暴雨的（rough sea/weather）（熟词僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: The sea grew rough without warning, and the little fishing boat pitched violently. （读后续写·海上遇险·环境描写）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ⑤rough it：将就着过艰苦简陋的生活（熟词僻义·固定搭配）
uncommonMeanings.example: For the whole camping trip we roughed it — no electricity, no running water — yet those star-lit nights taught me more about happiness than any comfort ever had. （读后续写·野营·感悟升华）

posExamples.sentence: His rough palms, hardened by decades of labour in the fields, closed gently around mine, and in that instant I understood every sacrifice my grandfather had never spoken of. （读后续写·亲情·细节描写）
I know the past semester has been a rough ride for many of us, so I am writing to invite you to the stress-relief workshop our Student Union has organized for this Friday. （应用文·邀请信）

Admittedly, any worthwhile pursuit involves rough patches; it is precisely how we respond to these setbacks, rather than the setbacks themselves, that determines how far we can eventually go. （议论文·挫折与成长）
According to our rough estimate, more than two hundred students would benefit from the proposed reading corner, which makes the project well worth the investment. （应用文·建议信·数据支撑）

wordForms.other: 反义词 smooth(光滑的/顺利的)；副词 roughly 一词两义：修饰数字=大约(roughly 200)，修饰动作=粗暴地(push roughly)；固定搭 rough it 过苦日子(it 不可省)、roughly speaking 大致而言；易错：rough 读 /rʌf/，-ough 发 /ʌf/

idioms.idiom: take the rough with the smooth
idioms.translation: 既能享福也能吃苦；好坏都接受
idioms.example: Growing up means learning to take the rough with the smooth — celebrating the victories, yes, but also shaking hands with failure and thanking it for the lesson. （议论文·成长态度）

idioms.translation: 外表粗犷但本质优秀的人；未经雕琢的璞玉
idioms.example: The new transfer student, silent and awkward at first, turned out to be a rough diamond whose paintings later won the national art competition. （读后续写·人物反转）

idioms.idiom: give sb. a rough ride / have a rough ride
idioms.translation: 让某人吃苦头；经历艰难
idioms.example: Sometimes parents forget that growing up is a rough ride, and what teenagers need most is not criticism but a patient ear. （议论文·亲子关系）

collocations.translation: 【课件】艰难的经历/时期（= difficult, hard）
collocations.example: Growing up is a rough ride. 成长是一段颠簸艰难的旅程。He's had a really rough time recently. 他最近过得很艰难。

collocations.translation: 【课件】大致的猜测/估计（not exact 不确切）
collocations.example: There were about 20 people there, at a rough guess. 粗略估计，那里大约有20人。

collocations.translation: 【课件】粗糙的（not smooth 不光滑）
collocations.example: The skin on her hands was hard and rough. 她手上的皮肤又硬又粗糙。

collocations.translation: 【课件】繁重的体力活（the hard physical work）
collocations.example: We'll get someone in to do the rough work. 我们会找人来干粗重的体力活。

collocations.translation: 一段艰难的经历（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Sometimes they forget that growing up is a rough ride. 有时他们忘了，成长本就是一段颠簸的旅程。
Their friendship hit a rough patch after the quarrel. 争吵之后他们的友谊陷入了一段低谷。
Can you give me a rough idea of the cost? 你能大致说说要花多少钱吗？

collocations.translation: 过苦日子，将就着过简陋生活
collocations.example: We roughed it for a week with no electricity. 我们没电将就着过了一周苦日子。
She polished the rough draft of her speech late into the night. 她熬夜打磨演讲的草稿。
His rough, calloused palms told of years of labour. 他粗糙长茧的手掌诉说着多年的劳作。

collocations.translation: 汹涌的大海；恶劣的天气
collocations.example: Despite the rough weather, the rescue team pressed on, their determination burning brighter than the storm was dark. （读后续写·救援·意志）

collocations.translation: 对某人苛刻；使某人难受
collocations.example: Moving to a new city was rough on him at first, yet each small kindness slowly rebuilt his confidence. （读后续写·适应新环境）
Roughly speaking, students who read for pleasure outperform their peers in almost every subject. （议论文·阅读的价值）

synonyms.translation: 光滑的；顺利的（反义辨析）
synonyms.example: The road turned from rough to smooth after the bend. 转过弯后，路面由崎岖变得平坦。
synonyms.usage: smooth 是 rough 的核心反义词：既指表面光滑(a smooth surface)，也指过程顺利(go smoothly)；rough 则表粗糙/颠簸，二者句法位置相同，常成对出现(take the rough with the smooth)

synonyms.example: It was a tough decision, but she boarded the train toward her dream. （读后续写·离别与追梦）
synonyms.usage: tough 强调难度大、需要毅力，也可形容人坚强；rough 更强调过程颠簸不顺、体验不适，二者作定语常可互换(a tough/rough time)

synonyms.example: The harsh winter tested the villagers. （读后续写·环境反衬）
synonyms.usage: harsh 侧重严厉、无情（气候、批评、条件）；rough 侧重不平坦、艰难但语气稍轻

synonyms.example: The uneven mountain path forced us to slow down. （读后续写·徒步·哲理）
synonyms.usage: uneven 仅指表面不平或分布不均，为中性描述；rough 兼指粗糙的手感与艰难的经历

advancedExpressions.example: 加 -ly 变副词 roughly，加 -ness 变名词 roughness，加 -en 变动词 roughen(使变粗糙)，同类 harden/soften/widen。

definitionEn:
(1) n. the failure or end of a relationship, discussion, or system
(2) n. an occasion when a vehicle or machine stops working
(3) n. a serious mental or physical collapse caused by stress or overwork

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ②【课件】（机器/车辆的）故障，抛锚（a machine stops working）
uncommonMeanings.example: Always carry a phone with you in case you have a breakdown on the freeway. 随身带手机以防在高速上抛锚。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ③【课件】（精神）崩溃（a period of mental illness）

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?

definitionEn:

(2) adj. happening or doing something often; frequent
(3) adj. usual or habitual; normal in size or type
(4) adj. evenly shaped or arranged; (grammar) following the standard pattern

uncommonMeanings.meaning: ①有规律的，定时的（间隔均等，遵循规律）（at regular intervals；regular check-ups）

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from their point of view.
readingExamples: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from their point of view.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. relaxed and quiet; not angry, nervous or upset
(2) adj. (of the sea) without big waves; (of weather) without wind
(3) vt. to make someone feel more relaxed and less emotional
(4) n. a peaceful and quiet state or period

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （人）平静的，镇静的，沉着的
uncommonMeanings.example: Try to stay calm when others panic. 别人恐慌时你要设法保持镇静。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使平静，使镇静
uncommonMeanings.example: The music calmed the crying baby. 音乐让哭闹的婴儿平静下来。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 平静，宁静（可数/不可数）
uncommonMeanings.example: An eerie calm settled over the campsite before the storm broke — the birds had stopped singing, and even the leaves seemed to hold their breath. （读后续写·暴风雨前·环境渲染）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （海面）风平浪静的；（天气）无风的
uncommonMeanings.example: By dawn the sea lay calm again, glittering innocently, as if it had entirely forgotten the fury with which it had tossed our boat all night. （读后续写·海上历险·拟人）

posExamples.sentence: Though her heart was hammering against her ribs, Sarah forced herself to sound calm as she dialed the emergency number, knowing that panic was a luxury the injured hiker could not afford. （读后续写·急救场景·内外反差）
The old teacher's steady voice calmed the frightened children the way a lighthouse calms lost ships, guiding them one by one out of the smoke-filled building. （读后续写·火灾疏散·明喻）
In my view, staying calm in the face of setbacks is not a natural gift but a trainable skill, one that every exam, every failure and every awkward moment offers us a chance to practise. （议论文·情绪管理）
Should you feel anxious before the interview, I recommend breathing deeply for one minute, which has been proven to calm the nerves and clear the mind remarkably well. （应用文·建议信）

wordForms.other: 构词法：calm + -ness → calmness（形容词加 -ness 变名词）；calm + -ly → calmly（形容词加 -ly 变副词）。词类活用：calm 一词同为 adj./v./n.。易错拼写：calm 中 l 不发音，读 /kɑːm/，别漏写 l。calm down 为可分动词短语：calm him down / calm down him✗，代词须放中间。

idioms.translation: 暴风雨前的平静；大乱前的暂时安宁
idioms.example: The house was unusually quiet that evening — the calm before the storm, for none of us knew the letter lying on the table would change our family forever. （读后续写·悬念铺垫）
While the other contestants fidgeted backstage, Amy remained calm, cool and collected, mentally rehearsing her opening line one last time. （读后续写·比赛·人物对比）

collocations.example: Take a minute to calm down and understand the situation from their point of view. 花一分钟平静下来，从他们的角度理解这件事。
She took a deep breath to calm herself (down). 她深吸了一口气，使自己平静下来。
Please try to stay calm. The doctor will be here soon. 请努力保持镇静，医生很快就到。
He explained everything, speaking in a calm voice. 他以平静的语气把一切解释清楚。
Under pressure he stayed cool, calm and collected. 压力之下他依然冷静镇定。

collocations.phrase: take a minute to calm down
collocations.translation: 花一分钟平静下来（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down. 当你和父母意见不合时，花一分钟平静下来。
Her gentle voice calmed the frightened child. 她温柔的声音安抚了受惊的孩子。
She hummed a song to calm her nerves. 她哼着歌来平复紧张。
"Don't worry," Dad said in a calm voice. “别担心，”爸爸用平静的语气说。
A calm sea never made a skilled sailor. 风平浪静练不出好水手。
He stayed calm and composed under pressure. 他在压力下沉着冷静。
The teacher's words restored calm to the class. 老师的话让班级恢复了平静。
She radiated an air of calm amid the chaos. 混乱中她散发出一种平静。

synonyms.example: The peaceful village lay wrapped in morning mist. 宁静的村庄笼罩在晨雾里。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：peaceful 多形容环境、氛围安宁祥和；calm 既可形容环境，更常形容人临事不慌的心理状态。句法/搭配：peaceful place / peaceful atmosphere，作定语或表语。

synonyms.example: She remained composed during the interview. 面试时她保持镇定。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：composed 强调（尤指压力下）自我控制良好，语体更正式；calm 为通用词，也可指天气、海面。句法/搭配：remain / stay composed，常作表语。

synonyms.example: The mother's lullaby soothed the crying baby. 母亲的摇篮曲安抚了哭泣的婴儿。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：soothe 对应 calm 的动词用法，侧重轻柔地安抚疼痛或情绪；calm sb down 更口语、更直接。句法/搭配：soothe sb / soothe the pain，及物动词接宾语。

synonyms.example: We rowed across the tranquil lake at sunset. 日落时我们划过静谧的湖面。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：tranquil 为书面语，描绘诗意的静谧景色或心境；calm 使用范围最广、语气最中性。句法/搭配：a tranquil lake / scene，多作定语。

advancedExpressions.expression: calm down（平静下来/使平静）| calm sb down（使某人冷静）| calm oneself down（让自己平静）| calm one's nerves（镇定神经）| keep/stay/remain calm（保持镇静）
advancedExpressions.example: Take a minute to calm down, keep calm, and calm your nerves before you speak. 花一分钟平静下来、保持冷静、镇定情绪后再开口。

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·功能（保持镇静，可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: stay calm ≈ keep cool ≈ remain composed ≈ keep a level head
advancedExpressions.example: Whatever happens, stay calm / keep cool / remain composed. 无论发生什么，都要保持镇静。

advancedExpressions.expression: calm(adj.) → calmness(n.)；同类：kind→kindness, dark→darkness, ill→illness
advancedExpressions.example: Her calmness in the crisis impressed everyone. 危机中她的镇定令所有人印象深刻。

advancedExpressions.expression: the calmer you remain, the better/wiser ...
advancedExpressions.example: Remember: the calmer you remain during the argument, the wiser your words will be — and the sooner your parents will be ready to listen. （the 比较级句式+呼应主题）

advancedExpressions.expression: true calm lies not in ..., but in ...
advancedExpressions.example: True calm lies not in the absence of storms, but in the ability to find peace within them — a quality that separates the resilient from the fragile. （not...but 对比定义法+同位语升华）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was nervous but tried to be calm.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Her palms were damp and her legs threatened to betray her, yet she drew a slow, deliberate breath, letting a hard-won calm spread through her body like warmth from a winter fire. （读后续写·身体细节+明喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 身体化描写(damp palms / legs betray her)代替直白的 nervous + 动作分解(drew a slow breath) + 明喻(like warmth from a winter fire)

sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from their point of view.
readingExamples: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from their point of view.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. to become quiet and relaxed after being angry, excited or upset
(2) phr. to make someone stop feeling angry, excited or upset
(3) phr. (of a situation) to become less tense or troubled

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （人）（愤怒/激动/恐慌后）平静下来，冷静下来（不及物）
uncommonMeanings.example: Please calm down and tell me what happened. 请冷静下来，告诉我发生了什么。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使某人平静下来（及物，calm sb down）
uncommonMeanings.example: Nothing could calm the baby down. 什么都没法让婴儿平静下来。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （局势/事态）平息下来，缓和
uncommonMeanings.example: The situation soon calmed down. 局势很快平息了下来。

posExamples.sentence: "Calm down and tell me exactly what happened," Mum said softly, kneeling to my eye level, and somehow her unhurried voice untangled the panic knotted in my chest. （读后续写·母女对话·安抚）
When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down before responding; a pause of sixty seconds, brief as it is, can spare a family an evening of cold silence. （应用文·建议信）
Psychologists point out that the ability to calm down quickly after a conflict is a stronger predictor of healthy relationships than the ability to avoid conflict altogether. （议论文·情绪管理·引证）
It took the frightened little boy a long while to calm down, but once the volunteer produced a paper plane from her pocket, a watery smile finally broke through his tears. （读后续写·志愿服务·破涕为笑）

wordForms.other: calm down 为可分（separable）短语动词：宾语是代词时必须放中间——calm him down（√）/ calm down him（✗）；宾语是名词时放中间或末尾均可——calm the baby down / calm down the baby。不及物用法（人/事态平静）无宾语：He calmed down.

collocations.example: Take a minute to calm down and understand the situation from their point of view. 花一分钟平静下来，从他们的角度理解这件事。

collocations.phrase: take a minute to calm down

collocations.example: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down. 当你和父母意见不合时，花一分钟平静下来。
Grandpa's old tune calmed the baby down. 爷爷的老曲子让婴儿平静下来。

collocations.phrase: calm down a bit / a little
collocations.example: Once the crowd calmed down a bit, the host went on. 人群稍微平静后，主持人继续讲。

collocations.phrase: take a deep breath and calm down
collocations.example: Take a deep breath and calm down before the exam. 考试前深呼吸，冷静下来。
After the talk, things gradually calmed down at home. 谈过之后，家里渐渐平静了。

collocations.phrase: wait for sb. to calm down
collocations.example: Wise parents wait for their child to calm down. 明智的父母会等孩子冷静下来。

synonyms.example: The students finally settled down when the film began. 电影开始时学生们终于安静了下来。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：settle down 侧重从喧闹归于安静或生活安定下来；calm down 侧重从愤怒、激动、恐慌等强烈情绪中恢复平静。句法/搭配：可作不及物短语，settle down to work。

synonyms.example: Let's both cool off before we talk again. 我们都先冷静下来再谈。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：cool down/off 特指怒气消退，口语色彩浓，也可指物理降温；calm down 适用范围更广，涵盖紧张、兴奋、悲伤等各种情绪。句法/搭配：cool down 可及物可不及物。

synonyms.example: She closed her eyes to compose herself before going on stage. 上台前她闭眼镇定了一下。
synonyms.usage: 语义差别：compose oneself 为正式书面语，强调有意识地整理情绪、恢复仪态；calm down 为日常通用表达。句法/搭配：须接反身代词 compose oneself。

advancedExpressions.example: Take a minute to calm down, calm yourself down, and keep calm. 花一分钟平静下来、让自己冷静、保持镇静。

advancedExpressions.expression: calm down ≈ settle down ≈ cool down/off ≈ compose oneself（须接反身）
advancedExpressions.example: Give her time to calm down / cool off / settle down. 给她时间冷静下来。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·可分短语动词代词位置

translation: 看法；视线；景色；把…视为；观看
sub_section: Article: Strangers under the same roof?
original_sentence: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from their point of view.
readingExamples: When you disagree with your parents, take a minute to calm down and try to understand the situation from their point of view.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a personal opinion, belief or attitude about something
(2) n. what you can see from a particular place, especially beautiful scenery
(3) n. the ability to see something from a particular place; sight
(4) vt. to think about or consider someone or something in a particular way
(5) vt. to look at or watch something, especially carefully or formally

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】理解方式，观念（way of understanding）
uncommonMeanings.example: The traditional view was that marriage was meant to last. 传统的观念是结成夫妻就要白头到老。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 看法，观点，见解
uncommonMeanings.example: In my view, both sides are partly right. 在我看来，双方都各有道理。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 视野，视线（come into view / block one's view）
uncommonMeanings.example: The lights of a farmhouse came into view through the fog. 农舍的灯光透过雾映入眼帘。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 景色，风景（从某处望出去看到的具体景象）
uncommonMeanings.example: The room has a fine view of the lake. 这房间能看到湖景。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 把……看作，认为（view A as B）
uncommonMeanings.example: We view it as a great chance. 我们把它看作一个大好机会。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 观看，参观，查看（房屋、展品等，较正式）
uncommonMeanings.example: Visitors may view the works in the gallery. 参观者可在展厅观看作品。

posExamples.sentence: Standing at the summit, we drank in the breathtaking view below — ribbons of river silvering the valley — and every blister on my feet suddenly seemed a small price to pay. （读后续写·登山·先抑后扬）
I am writing to share my views on the proposed mobile-phone policy: while I support limiting phone use in class, a total ban, in my view, would go a step too far. （应用文·意见信）
Instead of viewing failure as a wall that blocks our way, we would be wiser to view it as a mirror that shows us exactly where improvement is needed. （议论文·失败观·对比隐喻）
When you disagree with your parents, try to understand the situation from their point of view first; the same mountain, after all, looks entirely different from the other side. （议论文·换位思考·类比）

wordForms.noun: view / viewer (观众，观看者) / viewing (观看；参观)
wordForms.other: viewpoint (n. 观点，视角) / preview (n./v. 预览) / review (n./v. 复习，评论) / interview (n./v. 面试，采访)。构词法：view + point → viewpoint（合成词）；pre-（预先）/ re-（重新，回顾）/ inter-（在……之间）+ view 构成派生词。搭配注意：view A as B 与 regard A as B 中 as 不可省。

idioms.example: In view of the approaching storm, the sports meeting scheduled for tomorrow will be postponed until further notice. （应用文·通知）

idioms.idiom: with a view to doing sth.
idioms.example: Our school has launched a buddy programme with a view to helping new students adapt to campus life more smoothly. （应用文·介绍信/新闻报道）

idioms.translation: 在……众目睽睽之下，完全看得见的地方
idioms.example: In full view of the whole class, Tom walked up and admitted the broken window was his doing — and the room, instead of laughing, burst into applause. （读后续写·诚实担当·反转）
Reading novels told from a stranger's point of view quietly trains us in empathy, the very skill our divided world needs most. （议论文·阅读的意义）

collocations.translation: 【课件】从某人的观点/角度来看（= in one's view / opinion）
collocations.example: Try to understand the situation from their point of view. 试着从他们的角度理解这件事。
From my point of view, the proposal is practical. 在我看来，这个提议很实际。
His views on the subject were well known. 他对这个问题的看法众所周知。
We take the view that it would be wrong to blame him. 我们认为责怪他是不对的。

collocations.translation: 【课件】鉴于，考虑到（= considering; because of）
collocations.example: In view of the manager's poor health, the meeting will be put off. 鉴于经理身体欠佳，会议将被推迟。

collocations.phrase: come into view / be in view
collocations.translation: 【课件】进入视野，映入眼帘 / 在视野内
collocations.example: A baby lion suddenly came into view. 一头幼狮突然映入眼帘。
We can have a good view of the Bund from here. 我们在这里可以饱览外滩风光。
Are you interested in the room with a sea view? 您对那间海景房感兴趣吗？
Sanitary workers are often viewed as the angels on the road. 清洁工人常被视为马路上的天使。
We welcome the exchange of views whenever doubts arise. 每当有疑问时，我们欢迎交流观点。

collocations.translation: 从他们的角度（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Try to understand the situation from their point of view. 试着从他们的角度理解这件事。
The paintings are on view until Sunday. 这些画展出到周日。
In my view, the plan needs more thought. 在我看来，这计划还需再想想。
Don't view failure as an end. 别把失败看作终点。
We exchanged views on the new rule. 我们就新规定交换了意见。
I hold the view that reading changes lives. 我认为阅读能改变人生。

collocations.translation: 令人惊叹的/全景的景色
collocations.example: The deck offers a panoramic view of the city. 观景台可俯瞰全城。
The sea came into view as the train turned. 火车转弯时，大海映入眼帘。
A tall man blocked my view of the stage. 一个高个子挡住了我看舞台的视线。
